focus.note: Some verbs and adjectives always go with one small word. Learn the pair together: worry about, afraid of.

tfn.s: Katja Kokko has been in charge of the study for a shorter time than Lea Pulkkinen was.
tfn.why: Pulkkinen led it from 1968 to 2012, while Kokko has led it only since 2013.

tfn.s: Identity was measured at more ages than mental wellbeing was.

focus.note: Adjectives and verbs often need a fixed preposition. Check the word before the gap, not the one after it.

focus.note: At this level the preposition is fixed to a whole phrase: tantamount to, contingent on, fraught with. Learn each phrase as one block.

items.s: Claiming that identity work cures anxiety would be tantamount ____ overstating the evidence.
Any claim about causation is contingent ____ evidence that the researchers did not collect.
Studies that rely on self-reports are often fraught ____ bias.
Some adults, in defiance ____ social expectations, change careers at fifty.
A single study is a starting point, not a licence ____ drawing firm conclusions.

speak.title: Role-play: a big change at forty
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Your friend wants to leave a safe job and start something new at forty. You're worried about money and risk. Ask at least two questions before you give your opinion.

b.text: You want to change your life: a new job, a new city or a new hobby. Explain why it matters to you and how you'll manage the risks. Try to persuade your friend.

phrases: I've been thinking about doing something different.
I'm not sure it's the right time.
What would you do about money?
I know it's a risk, but I'd regret not trying.
You're still working out what you want, aren't you?
Let's agree to try it for six months.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did the worried friend change their mind, and what helped?
